expectations.text: Applies the right law: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (not the federal PDPL, not DIFC law), overseen by the ADGM Office of Data Protection / Commissioner
expectations.evidence: "ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (as amended), enforced by the ADGM Office of Data Protection / Commissioner of Data Protection — a GDPR-modeled regime independent of the UAE federal PDPL."

expectations.text: States the deadline correctly: notify the Commissioner within 72 HOURS of becoming aware of the breach, and notify affected data subjects where there is high risk to them
expectations.evidence: "within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk"; "If the breach is likely to result in a high risk... you must also notify the affected data subjects without undue delay".

expectations.text: Covers incident mechanics: assess scope (encryption status of the laptop matters to risk), contain (remote wipe, credential rotation), preserve evidence, and document the incident and decision-making even if notification is judged unnecessary
expectations.evidence: "determine what data was on the laptop, whether it was encrypted/password-protected/remotely wipeable, and whether remote wipe was executed successfully" (assess+contain); "start the incident log" (preserve evidence); "Regardless of whether the breach meets the notification threshold, you're expected to document all breaches internally (facts, effects, remedial action)" (explicitly covers documenting even if notification is judged unnecessary). Credential rotation specifically not named, but core mechanics are covered.

expectations.text: Notes the parallel regulator: as an FSRA-regulated asset manager, operational-incident expectations to FSRA run alongside the DP notification — and the answer must not cite CBUAE
expectations.evidence: Dedicated 'Track 2 — FSRA regulatory notification' section describing parallel FSRA incident reporting; CBUAE is never mentioned anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: Includes follow-through: root-cause remediation (encryption, MDM), RoPA/security-policy updates, and annual-notification standing with the ODP
expectations.evidence: "Root cause and remediation: Device encryption policy, mobile device management (remote wipe capability), and physical security controls should be reviewed..." covers encryption/MDM, but RoPA updates and annual-notification standing with the ODP are never mentioned.
